meta.title: OxideTerm — AI-native workspace for remote servers
meta.description: An AI-native workspace for remote servers: SSH terminals, SFTP, remote desktop, port forwarding, trzsz, lightweight editing, local shell, and OxideSens AI. No bundled Electron, no telemetry, and pure-Rust SSH without OpenSSL/libssh2.

hero.headline: AI-native workspace for remote servers
hero.tagline: Native GPUI. No bundled WebView. No telemetry. No subscription. BYOK-first. Pure-Rust SSH without OpenSSL/libssh2.
hero.subtitle: Connect once, then keep terminals, SFTP, remote desktops, port forwarding, transfers, lightweight editing, local shells, and OxideSens AI in one local-first desktop app.
hero.mock_ai: OxideSens sees terminal, files, and server context

features.title: Built Different
features.rust_ssh_desc: Built on russh with the ring crypto backend. The SSH stack has no C, OpenSSL, or libssh2 dependency and is compiled entirely in auditable Rust.
features.native_desc: A 50–70 MB native GPUI desktop package built in Rust. No Electron wrapper and no system WebView runtime; the terminal is rendered directly by the GPU-backed native UI.
features.allinone_desc: Terminal, SFTP, RDP/VNC, IDE, AI assistant, port forwarding, and plugins — unified in a single window. No more juggling tools.
features.reconnect_desc: Network drops? OxideTerm probes your old connection for 30 seconds before reconnecting. Your vim, htop, and yazi sessions survive.
features.proxyjump_desc: Chain unlimited jump hosts with built-in topology graph. No SSH config needed — set up multi-hop connections visually.
features.plugins_desc: Process, Wasm, and manifest-only plugins add declarative native surfaces without loading JavaScript into a WebView.

comparison.title: Why OxideTerm?
comparison.subtitle: Not just a terminal. An AI-native workspace for remote servers that stays local‑first.
comparison.pain_1: Remote server work is split across too many tools
comparison.answer_1: AI-native remote-server workspace — terminals, SFTP, RDP/VNC, port forwarding, trzsz, lightweight IDE, monitoring, and OxideSens AI under one node
comparison.pain_2: You still need a local shell
comparison.answer_2: Integrated local shell — zsh/bash/fish/pwsh/WSL2 beside SSH sessions, so local and remote tasks share one UI
comparison.pain_3: Remote file editing needs another dedicated development tool
comparison.answer_3: Built-in IDE — native GPUI editor over SFTP with tree-sitter highlighting for 36 languages and an optional remote agent
comparison.answer_4: Multiplexing — one SSH connection shared across terminal, SFTP, forwarding, and IDE
comparison.answer_5: russh 0.61 — pure Rust SSH compiled against ring. Zero C dependencies
comparison.answer_6: Native GPUI — a Rust desktop app without an Electron or WebView runtime layer
comparison.pain_7: You do not want telemetry or app subscriptions
comparison.answer_7: Zero tracking, zero core app subscription — SSH/SFTP/port forwarding/local shell need no OxideTerm account or subscription; Cloud Sync remains opt-in
comparison.answer_8: Encrypted at rest — OS keychain for passwords, ChaCha20-Poly1305 + Argon2id for .oxide exports. Nothing in plain text
comparison.pain_9: You want AI without a platform account
comparison.answer_9: BYOK-first OxideSens AI — inspect saved connections, live SSH sessions, terminal buffers, SFTP paths, settings, and knowledge base entries, then perform approved workspace actions

showcase.title: See It in Action
showcase.terminal_desc: Split panes, broadcast input, GPU-backed GPUI rendering, font ligatures, built-in themes, session recording, and command palette.
showcase.sftp_desc: Dual-pane file browser with drag-and-drop, smart preview for images, video, code, and hex. Transfer queue with progress tracking.
showcase.ide_desc: Native GPUI editor with tree-sitter syntax support for 36 languages, a Git-aware file tree, conflict handling, and an integrated terminal.
showcase.forwarding_desc: Local (-L), Remote (-R), and Dynamic SOCKS5 (-D) forwarding. Lock-free I/O, auto-restore on reconnect, death reporting.
showcase.ai_desc: OxideSens is the BYOK AI for your remote-server workspace. It treats saved connections, live SSH sessions, terminal buffers, SFTP paths, settings, and knowledge base entries as targets, then performs approved actions without requiring an OxideTerm account.

tech.title: Under the Hood
tech.dual_plane_desc: SSH sessions, workspace state, and terminal surfaces run inside one native Rust application instead of crossing a WebSocket and IPC boundary.
tech.webgl_desc: The terminal is rendered by GPUI's GPU-backed native renderer, with adaptive rendering controls and a compatibility profile for lighter visual effects.
tech.pool_desc: One SSH connection shared across terminal, SFTP, forwarding, and IDE. Reference-counted pool with automatic cleanup.
tech.encryption_desc: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD with Argon2id KDF (256 MB memory, 4 iterations). OS keychain for passwords, Touch ID gate on macOS.
tech.i18n_desc: Full UI translation across 22 namespaces: English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, 한국어, Français, Deutsch, Español, Italiano, Português, Tiếng Việt.
tech.plugin_desc: Wasm and process plugins can contribute native tabs, sidebar panels, settings, commands, status items, shortcuts, and terminal hooks.

security.title: Security First
security.subtitle: Enterprise-grade protection without enterprise complexity.
security.encryption_desc: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD with Argon2id KDF (256 MB memory, 4 iterations) for .oxide encrypted exports.
security.keychain_desc: Passwords and API keys stored in macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service. Never in config files.
security.ssh_desc: russh 0.61 with ring crypto backend. Ed25519, RSA, ECDSA keys. ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-GCM cipher suites.
security.biometric_desc: Touch ID gates keychain access on macOS. Host key verification with Trust-On-First-Use (TOFU). Sensitive memory zeroized on drop.
security.zeroize_desc: All sensitive data — passwords, keys, decrypted payloads — is securely erased from memory via the zeroize crate. Drop handlers guarantee no lingering secrets.
security.ws_token_desc: Terminal I/O and workspace control stay inside the native Rust process, removing the old browser bridge and its session-token boundary.

legal.title: Compliance & Legal
legal.subtitle: OxideTerm is designed for legitimate system administration, development, and research. We take compliance seriously.
legal.network_desc: OxideTerm is a professional remote server management and terminal emulation tool. This software is intended solely for compliant system administration, network management, software development, and academic research. Users must strictly comply with all applicable laws and regulations when using SSH tunneling or port forwarding features. Any use of this software for unauthorized access to restricted resources or violation of cybersecurity regulations is strictly prohibited.
legal.ai_desc: OxideTerm stores AI conversation history on your device. When you make an AI request, the messages and any context you choose to include are sent directly to the provider you configured and are handled under that provider's terms and privacy policy. Local model providers can keep this traffic on your machine. OxideTerm does not operate an AI relay or collect these conversations. Use AI features only with data you are authorized to share and in accordance with applicable laws and provider terms.
legal.data_desc: Core work stays local and needs no OxideTerm account. Credentials stay in your system keychain; Cloud Sync and AI connect only when you choose and configure a provider.
legal.license_desc: This software is distributed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL-3.0). OxideTerm previously used PolyForm Noncommercial and moved to GPL-3.0 to avoid source-available traps, noncommercial ambiguity, and no-competition riders. Public code is not automatically open source: no-redistribution, no-repackaging, no-competing-products, or platform-approval riders turn it into source-available branding. OxideTerm adds none of those riders.
legal.disclaimer: This page is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Users are responsible for ensuring their use of OxideTerm complies with all applicable local and international laws.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: OxideTerm is open source under the GPL-3.0 license. Free for everyone — personal, educational, and commercial use. Derivative works must also be open sourced under GPL-3.0.
faq.q2: Which SSH authentication methods are supported?
faq.a2: Password, private key (Ed25519, RSA, ECDSA), keyboard-interactive 2FA, agent forwarding, certificates, and SSH Agent.
faq.a3: OxideTerm is local-first: core SSH workflows work without an OxideTerm account. Credentials stay in your OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service), and exported configs use ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption. Cloud Sync and AI contact only the providers you choose after configuring them.
faq.a4: Yes. OxideTerm is local-first. Core SSH workflows — SSH, SFTP, port forwarding, local shell, saved connections, and settings — do not require an OxideTerm account or subscription. AI needs your configured provider API when you choose to use it.
faq.q5: What do I need for AI features?
faq.a5: Bring your own API key (BYOK). OxideTerm supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Provider usage fees are between you and that provider; OxideTerm does not require an app subscription for core SSH workflows or OxideSens AI.
faq.q6: Why doesn't OxideTerm's SSH stack use libssh2 or OpenSSL?
faq.a6: Three reasons. First, memory safety: OpenSSL's C codebase has produced critical CVEs like Heartbleed — Rust's ownership model eliminates that entire class of bug. Second, zero deployment friction: libssh2 requires each target platform to have C dev headers and the system OpenSSL matching in version (1.0 vs 1.1 vs 3.0 have incompatible ABIs); russh ships as pure Rust source and Cargo handles everything. Third, async-native performance: libssh2 is a blocking C API that needs wrapper glue for Tokio; russh is async-first with zero FFI boundary in the hot path. The result is a Rust-native SSH stack without an OpenSSL runtime dependency and with a cryptographic implementation that remains practical to audit.

testimonial.quote: I built OxideTerm because I wanted one tool that actually does everything — SSH, SFTP, port forwarding, code editing — without feeling heavy or asking for a subscription. The tech choices (pure-Rust SSH, binary wire protocol, ChaCha20 encryption) aren't there to show off; they're just what made sense when you want something fast, portable, and correct. It's a solo project, so it won't be perfect, but I'd rather ship something honest than something polished with corners cut.
